Great talking Friday. We're a go on the 6-week paid pilot. I've looped in our platform team. A few things from our side before we sign:

Marcus

questions.storyline: The Northwind Logistics pilot deal. Sam Rivera, technical solo founder of Halcyon (a dev-tools startup), with cofounder Priya Nair, runs a paid pilot of Halcyon's product with Northwind Logistics. The customer contact is Marcus Vance, who emails from BOTH marcus.vance@northwind.com (his primary) and mvance@northwind.com (an alias that shows up partway through the thread) — the same person across handles. The pilot timeline is deliberately fragmented across sources: the Gmail thread carries kickoff logistics, pricing/procurement, and Marcus's stakeholder feedback; the two Halcyon-calendar meetings (kickoff 2026-05-06, mid-pilot check-in 2026-06-05) carry the meeting anchors and attendee lists; Sam's notes carry his own action summaries and a pricing decision; and iMessage with Priya carries the operational reminders. The DROPPED COMMITMENT — Sam promised Marcus a SOC2 security addendum doc — exists ONLY in iMessage: Sam tells Priya on 2026-05-18 he committed to send it by Friday, Priya pings him again on 2026-06-03 ("still not in the Northwind thread"), and it is never closed. No email or note ever mentions the SOC2 addendum, so an email+notes-only reader misses that Northwind's procurement is blocked on it. Other commitments (Priya owns trial workspace setup — closed; Marcus owns internal stakeholder sign-off — in progress; Sam owns the pricing quote — sent) resolve in email/notes, making the SOC2 gap the one open thread that only surfaces by reading iMessage AND cross-referencing the email thread where it's conspicuously absent.
